quote_text:
Yeah, I mean, you know, obviously,  it definitely wasn’t the scoreline  
that we were hoping for. You know, had  the game finished in a nil-nil draw,  
I don’t think there would have been too  many complaints from myself or from Derek.
You know, we had one or two half-chances. I  actually thought we got into more dangerous  
areas than Kilmarnock over the  piece but just lacked a little  
bit of quality in the final  third with that final ball.
Really unlucky at nil-nil—Sam Delby has  a header that comes off the crossbar.
But, you know, the real frustration for us is  the manner of the goal that we concede. You know,  
I’ve watched it now numerous times  from lots of different angles,  
and I can’t understand how the  guys in the VAR studio don’t  
rule that one out or at least ask the  referee to come and view the monitor.
And, you know, Jack Walton is trying to get  off the ground, but it’s impossible because  
the Kilmarnock forward’s arm is right across  his face before he heads it into the goal.
Very similar, I would say, to the one at  Fir Park a few weeks ago when, you know,  
Motherwell scored, but it was ruled  out for a foul on Butland at the time.
And I think, you know, that’s the bit  that annoys us all is that, you know,  
we’re looking for that bit of  consistency across the board.
And, you know, for me, that goal shouldn’t stand.
Have you had an explanation  from the referee as to why?
No, because I don’t think the referee’s  had a chance to see it back yet either.
You know, I think, as I said, the guys in  the VAR studio can see it from all angles,  
and, you know, I just don’t  understand how that’s not ruled out.
I don’t think there would have been too  many complaints from Kilmarnock either  
had it been chalked off. It’s a  foul as far as we’re concerned.
And, you know, it makes it even harder  to accept because it’s cost us points.
Jack’s in there, adamant that he was fouled?
Yeah, well, we’ve seen it  back—it’s a foul. You know,  
those types of free kicks on goalkeepers get  given every week up and down the country.
You know, I am quite old-school when  it comes to goalkeepers. You know,  
I do think they’re overprotected at times.
But I don’t think there’s a great deal Jack  Walton can do in that situation. You know,  
he’s got his eyes on the ball, he’s  just about to jump and try and catch it,  
and the right arm of the Kilmarnock  forward comes across his face.
And then the Killie player  gets the head on the ball.
So, as I said, it’s consistency.  We’ve seen goals like that chalked  
out over the season. This one today has cost us.
That’s the same official as a couple  of weeks ago that you also had the  
complaint about not going over to the  monitor in the Motherwell match. I mean,  
is that disappointing—it’s  the same person involved?
No, I’m not going to blame the referee. You know,  the guys in the VAR studio are the ones that need  
to decide whether those big decisions merit  the referee going and looking at the monitor.
I always believe that the referee  should have the final say,  
especially in those types of decisions  that are game-changing decisions.
I always believe the referee should get�� the opportunity to go and look at it,  
and then if he gives it, then fair enough.
But, I think when David Dickinson watches it back,  
I think he’ll be in agreement with us that  it’s a foul all day long on the goalie.
Ian Campbell in from the start—how  do you feel like he got on?
Yeah, I mean, you know, it’s Alan’s first  start in a considerable period of time,  
but he’s a fit boy anyway.
You know, I thought he added some real  good energy in the middle of the pitch.
The game was scrappy, you know. It was—you know  what you’re going to get when you come down here.
I don’t think too many of us have  witnessed too many really attractive,  
entertaining games of football on this pitch.
You know, I don’t think Derek or his  players particularly enjoy it either.
But, I thought it was a real battle. You know,  
I didn’t think there were any real great  moments of quality in the game from either team.
And, you know, if it was a moment of quality that,  
you know, Kilmarnock scored  from, then we could accept it.
But we can’t accept that one  in the manner that it was.
It should have been a nil-nil game,  and we should have taken a point,  
and you know, that would have probably  been justified over the whole piece.  
Kai and M. Thompson just out of the squad  due to the amount of options you’ve got?
Yeah, basically.
Thanks.
title: Jim Goodwin’s FULL Press Conference | Kilmarnock 1-0 Dundee United
